newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil may benefit from Asian devaluations-cenbank.
newsitem.headline: Brazil may benefit from Asian devaluations-cenbank.

text.p: Brazil's Central Bank does not envisage any negative fallout from the currency woes of some Asian economies and in fact, believes Latin America's largest country may even be boosted, a spokeswoman said.

Quoting Director of International Affairs Gustavo Franco, the spokeswoman said a de facto devaluation Friday by the Philippines and Thailand's trendsetting devaluation of the bhat two weeks ago might draw added foreign investment to Brazil.
"He (Franco) doesn't think there will be any repercussions in Brazil. He thinks it might even have a favourable effect because these are competing markets," she said.
"Foreign capital may decide to come here instead," she added."

Through the spokeswoman, Franco noted that he found it "interesting" that Thailand and the Philippines had better risk ratings from the international agencies than Brazil. Franco has led a long-running Brazilian push for a better rating.

He said he believed the balance of payments current account problems of some Asian countries were partly due to fierce competition for exports and foreign investment by China, a problem Brazil did not directly suffer from.
"He doesn't see a crisis," the spokeswoman said. "He sees these moves as preventive measures by these countries which won't have great consequences."

Thailand's move two weeks ago rattled Asian currency markets. When Manila's Central Bank announced it was allowing the peso to move in a wider range to the dollar, the currency promptly plunged 11.5 percent in value.
Analysts say Brazil shares many of the problems facing Asian economies like Thailand, such as a widening current account gap and an overvalued currency.
But Brazil's current account deficit is several percentage points narrower and its Central Bank has a $59 billion war chest of foreign reserves to scare off any speculators.
Brazil's spot foreign exchange market barely blinked at the Philippines news, but the futures contracts on the dollar traded more nervously, traders said.
